parties:
Md Nurul Islam ----- Defendan Respondent-Petitioner  
VS.
Nur Ayesha Begum ----- Plaintiff-Appellant Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 4-11-1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge and 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Family Appeal No. 24 of 1993 reversing those dated 7-2-1993 passed by the Family Court and Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Patiya, Chittagong in Family Suit No. 46 of 1992 should not be set aside. 

 5. The trial Court after consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit in part and declared that the plaintiff is entitled to get only the prompt dower because the divorce was not legally effected due to the non compliance of service of notice to the Chairman under section 7(1) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree defendant-petitioner moved this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. I have perused the judgment and decree of the Courts below and also the records. 

 13. It is admitted that the plaintiff and defendant were legally wed couple and marriage was held on 12-4-1988 and there is no deference of opinion that the dower was fixed Taka 80,000 out of which Taka 21,000 was paid as gold ornaments. The rest was divided into two portion from which Taka 30,000 as prompt dower and Taka 29,000 as deferred dower. The trial Court decreed the prompt dower and opined that divorce not yet legally effected due to lack of initiative by the defendant under section 7 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961, so the plaintiff only can entitled to get her prompt dower. Whereas the appellate Court reversed the same. 

 28. Hadith No. 228. Narrated Sahl bin Sa'd As-Saidi: 'Uwaimir Al-Ajlani came to Asim bin Adi Al-Ansari and said to him, 'O Asim Suppose a man saw another man with his wife, would he kill him whereupon you would kill him; or what should he do? Please, O Asim, ask about this on my behalf." Asim asked Allah's Apostle about it. Allah's Apostle disliked that question and considered it disgraceful. What Asim heard from Allah's Apostle was hard on him. When 'Asim returned to his family, 'Uwaimir came to him and said 'O Asim! What did Allah's Apostle say to you?" Asim said to 'Uwaimir, "You never bring me any good. Allah's Appostile disliked the problem which I asked him about." 'Uwaimir said, "By Allah, I will not give up this matter until I ask the Prophet about it." So 'Uwaimir proceeded till he came to Allah's Apposite in the midst of people, and said, "O Allah's Apostle! If a man sees another man with his wife, would he kill him, whereupon you would kill him, or what would he do? Allah's Apostle said," Allah has revealed some decree as regards you and your wife's case. Go and bring her." So they carried out the process of Lian while I have present among the people with Allah's Apostle. When they had finished their Lian, 'Uwaimir said, "0 Allah's Apostle! If I should now keep her with me as a wife, then I have told a lie." So he divorced her thrice before Allah's Apostle ordered him. (Ibn Shihab said: So divorce was the tradition for all those who were involved in a case of Lian.) 

 35. From the above cited Quranic verses and Hadiths it appears that if a man accused his wife of illegal sexual intercourse Prophet Mohammad (Peace be upon him) made both of them take the oath of Tian and departed them each other. It is against human nature that the parties can live together happily after such an allegation. It also appears that the matter decided by the Prophet Mohammad (Peace be upon him) that he separated them from each other. According to Mullah's Mohammedan Law charge of lian does not of itself terminate the marriage. The marriage continuous until the decree is passed. In this case where husband accused charged his wife of adultery so in such a situation I find no alternative to pass an order of separation (divorce). 

 39. So the mother is the custodian of the minor son till he has completed the age of seven years. Considering the above section of law it is my view that the maintenance of the child must be paid by the defendant from 10-5-1992 to 6-10-1995. But the plaintiff did not claim the said maintenance of her child, she only claimed the maintenance of the child for two months i.e. Taka 400 and the appellate Court decreed the same. So I don't deserve any interference of the decision of the appellate Court though the plaintiff is entitled to get the maintenance of her child from 10-5-1992 to 6-10-1995 and plaintiff can claimed the same at any stage. 

 43. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is hereby upheld with above modification. The plaintiff opposite party is entitled to get not only her entire dower money but also with her iddat allowance without complying the provision of section 7 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961. And also the maintenance of the child fixed by the appellate Court.
